subject: Culture
title: The Honor Code
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Honor Code.

hook.text: In parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East, family honor can justify violence. Law often looks away.

buildup.text: Honor cultures tie personal worth to group perception. An insult to one member threatens all.

discovery.text: The American South has an honor-culture legacy too. Dueling persisted there long after the North abandoned it.

twist.text: Dignity cultures—common in northern Europe—locate worth inside the individual, not the group's opinion.

climax.text: Whether shame falls on you alone or your whole family shapes how an entire society polices behavior.

punchline.text: Honor is either yours to keep or yours to share.

quiz.question: What distinguishes a 'dignity culture' from an 'honor culture'?
options: Dignity cultures have no social norms
Worth is located in the individual, not the group
Dignity cultures value wealth over family
